essence: Writing down a fault before opening an object helps visitors contribute to its diagnosis at a Saturday repair room.
brief: The repair room asks each visitor to describe a fault on paper before work begins. A clock owner’s account pointed to a bent tooth, while a conversation about a lamp narrowed the problem to a loose switch. Visitors take the slips home to give the next volunteer a record.
understanding: The pencil is part of the repair process because the owner has observed the object in use. Volunteers begin by listening for a pattern that might guide inspection.
A once-per-turn click led to a bent tooth. A vague concern about a lamp needed another conversation before the owner and volunteer identified a loose switch.
The slip leaves with the object and can inform a future repair. The room keeps no central record, so the organisers have no basis for claiming that the method makes repairs last longer.
